terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation; with the accusative and infinitive
evidence: Caes. BG 1.27: eōs suum adventum exspectāre jussit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 9.13.2: hae mē litterae Dolābellae jubent ad prīstinās cōgitātiōnēs revertī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The ordinary verb: the person told stands in the accusative, what is to be done in the infinitive. Also of what the people enact: senātus dēcrēvit populusque jussit (Cic. Verr. 2.2.161, Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with the dative of the person and ut or nē with the subjunctive
evidence: Caes. BG 1.28.1: hīs, utī conquīrerent et redūcerent, imperāvit (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 2.32.3: quae imperārentur, facere dīxērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The command of someone in authority: a general, a master, a parent.

phrases.english: he ordered them to wait for his arrival

phrases.latin: hīs, utī conquīrerent et redūcerent, imperāvit
phrases.english: he ordered them to hunt the men out and bring them back
they said they would do what was ordered

sources: Lewis & Short: jubeo · Lewis & Short: impero
